bounds_volumes.name: NavBounds_Town
bounds_volumes.basis: 1040 m square CENTRED ON THE TOWN at (-210800, 278800), covering all 940 m of its extent with margin. NOT snapped to the 102400 cm chunk grid, and that is deliberate: the grid cell containing the plaza, [-3,2], carries 351.9 m of relief and covers only the SOUTH-WEST part of the town, so most of its voxel volume would be mountainside the town does not occupy. The chunk-grid alignment on the volume above existed so chunk actors would not straddle TILES -- that property comes from 102400 being an exact multiple of TileSizeUU 1600, and it survives here because these bounds are themselves multiples of 1600, asserted at measurement time. A town-centred box simply spans more chunk ACTORS, which R-NAVBUILD already records as arithmetic rather than a defect. Z is MEASURED: 625 downward collision traces on a 43 m lattice, foliage ignored so no trace lands on a canopy, found terrain from 12713.5 to 43013.0 cm with ZERO misses; the bounds add ~11 m below and ~20 m above, matching the convention of the volume above. That is a 334 m column -- 3,340 voxel rows per tile at CellHeight 10 cm against 1,750 for the spawn volume, 1.9x, and still 4.6x cheaper than sizing Z to the whole world. || NavBounds_TownEast below extends coverage outward from this volume's eastern edge. They SHARE the edge at x = -158400 rather than overlapping, so the pair is contiguous and an agent can cross between them.

bounds_volumes.name: NavBounds_TownEast
bounds_volumes.basis: 1040 m square sharing its western edge with NavBounds_Town at x = -158400, extending coverage OUTWARD from the basin. EAST WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, not by eye: the offline walkable-component prefilter, run over a 5 km box at the walk agent, reports the plaza's component reaching 2480 m (the sample limit) on bearings 0, 60, 75, 90, 120 and 150 degrees, and closing at 440-780 m on bearings 165-285. The prefilter is OPTIMISTIC so its OPEN verdicts are not trusted -- but its CLOSED verdicts are, and they rule out the western half. Bearing 0 is +X, so this volume covers the strongest open direction. Z is MEASURED: 625 traces on a 43 m lattice, foliage ignored, terrain 12713.5 to 30881.4 cm with ZERO misses; bounds add ~11 m below and ~20 m above, the same convention as the volumes above. That is a 214 m column against the town volume's 334 m -- this ground is gentler, which is why the component runs out through it. Bounds are multiples of TileSizeUU 1600, asserted at measurement time.

layers.name: Snow
layers._tiling_derivation: BRIEF 3 TASK 3, 2026-09-11. tiling_m is DERIVED, not chosen: the texel budget at hfov 90, 3840x2160, near 3 m gives 814.9 texels/m needed, so a 4096 albedo spans 4096/814.9 = 5.03 m at ~1 texel per render pixel. Every surface bound to a layer here is 4096 square (vendor manifest), so 5.03 applies to all three. macro_tiling_m 188.0 = 37.4x the tile, inside the ruled 20-50x band. PREVIOUS: Snow/Rock 4.0 -- that implies 1024 texels/m at 3 m, 26% short of what the camera resolves; Grass 2.1 with macro 98.7 (47x).
layers._tile_size_UNSTATED: R-TILE, RULED 2026-09-13: this layer KEEPS 5.03 and is tagged UNSTATED. Every other bound layer now tiles from its scan's own surface_tile_m, but ambientCG publishes NO physical size for Snow007A -- dimensionX/Y/Z read 0 from its own API, not merely absent from the shipped sidecar (REGISTER B3.11). So 5.03 here is the texel-budget ceiling standing in for a number the vendor does not provide, and the stretch factor is UNKNOWABLE rather than 1.00.
layers._surface_bind: RULED 2026-09-12: Snow006 -> Snow007A (ambientCG, CC0). BOUND because it is one of only TWO scans of eight that pass the 16-bit height gate; the six Megascans scans ship 8-bit JPEG Displacement and were REFUSED. Tile stays the DERIVED 5.03 m (texel_budget at the judgement camera), not the scan physical size, which ambientCG does not publish. NOTE: this bind is NOT OBSERVABLE at Bench_ground -- that station sits at 65 m and the snow line is 730 m, so the tiling and albedo tables cannot see it.

layers.name: Rock
layers._tiling_m_from_the_scan: RULED 2026-09-12b: tile this layer FROM 1.8 m. gray_rocks declares stated_size_m [1.8, 1.8] in its own vendor sidecar, so 1.8 shows the scan at ITS TRUE SIZE. The texel-budget figure below (5.03 m) is a CEILING, not a target: it is the largest tile that still resolves ~1 texel per render pixel at 3 m. Tiling at 5.03 would have STRETCHED a 1.8 m scan by 2.79x -- the stretch factor ASSETS.md row 167 records -- and rocks at 2.8x life size read as a texture rather than as ground. Tiling tighter costs nothing in sharpness: 4096/1.8 = 2276 texels/m, far above the 814.9 needed.

layers._sub_surface_removed: schema v1.26 (2026-09-12). REMOVED: {surface: Rock026, height_contrast: 0.35}, which was the SCREE/TALUS sub-surface selected by the variant map's G channel (make_variant_map.py:16). Scree is now a real LAYER with its own derived weight (weightmap channel B) and its own scan (rocks_ground_04). Keeping both would be TWO DERIVATIONS OF ONE PHYSICAL FACT -- derive_layer_weights' slope-plus-uphill-source mask and rock_scatter.talus_deposit -- which is NN19, and they cannot be reconciled by inspection because both are plausible. The weightmap's scree wins: R-LAYERS is locked on three independent strands and the eight weights sum to 1 by construction. The sub-surface mechanism was the documented workaround for 'the weightmap carries THREE'; that budget no longer binds.

layers.name: Scree

layers._no_macro_tiling: macro_tiling_m is ABSENT deliberately: it scales the legacy per-layer `texture` (schema v1.2) and this layer has none -- it is bound by `surface` alone. The validator REFUSES macro_tiling_m without texture, correctly: a scale factor with nothing to scale is an inert field that reads like a setting.

With the weightmap present these bounds do NOT drive the mask -- the baked B channel does, and it additionally requires a >40 deg cell within 60 m that is HIGHER, which no slope band alone can express.

layers._remainder_layer: ⛔ THIS LAYER MUST STAY LAST. schema v1.26, Brief 3 Task 3 (2026-09-12): the weightmap stores FOUR channels -- R=Snow G=Rock B=Scree A=ForestFloor -- and this layer (meadow) is the SHADER REMAINDER 1-(R+G+B+A), clamped at 0. LAYER ORDER IS CHANNEL ORDER: reordering this array silently repaints the world, and nothing downstream can detect it because every mask still sums to 1. The remainder is NOT stored, because a fifth channel would be a fifth number obliged to agree with four others and 8-bit quantisation guarantees it sometimes would not (NN24); derived in the shader the masks sum to 1 by construction. Coverage 25.17% = meadow 24.65 + gravel 0.52, the fold ASSERTED against w8b by `derive_layer_weights.py --expand` (measured gap 0.00392 = 1/255). The channel mapping itself lives ONCE, in make_landscape_material.WEIGHTMAP_CHANNELS; see RECIPES R-LAYERS5.

displacement._schema: v1.27 (Brief 7 Phase 1). Per-layer Nanite displacement amplitude in METRES, replacing the single global amplitude_m 0.4 that predated the Brief 3 per-layer 16-bit height scans. Keys MUST be exactly the material.layers names; the validator refuses the retired amplitude_m key and any key that is not a layer. The reducer displacement_spec uses the MAX value as the engine displacement_scaling.magnitude reference and the graph scales each layer's centred-height deviation by amplitude_layer/amplitude_ref, so a fully-mipped or map-less pixel still reads center and moves by nothing. NAME NOTE: the brief calls the remainder layer 'Meadow'; this world's remainder layer is named 'Grass' (R-LAYERS5: R=Snow G=Rock B=Scree A=ForestFloor, remainder=Grass derived in the shader) — Grass 0.03 IS the brief's Meadow 0.03.

height_blend._k_ruling: RULED 0.0 by Ryan 2026-09-24 (Brief 7 Phase 1 retry, step 1). The desk's k=4.0 SHATTERED the terrain into ~1-3 m cubic blocks: w*(h+eps)^k with k=4 sharpens the 1 m weightmap ramps to sub-texel steps (shading, not geometry -- r.Nanite.Tessellation 0 left it unchanged; LESSONS 2026-09-24). k=0 disables the reweight (identity), the positive control that lands per-layer displacement, R-TILE and GroundClutter without blocking. The power form is RETIRED on branch look-p1-heightblend in favour of a BOUNDED modulation w_i*(1 + a*(h_i-0.5)), a=0.6 (schema v1.29, field height_blend.a; validator will refuse k).
height_blend._schema: v1.28 (Brief 7 Phase 1 addendum). Height-weighted layer blend inside the weightmap composite -- the effect of LB_HeightBlend, which has no referent in M_Alpine8K (it is a LinearInterpolate composite over a baked weightmap, not a LandscapeLayerBlend). Each STORED layer's mask (Snow/Rock/Scree/ForestFloor) is scaled by (h_i + eps)**k, where h_i is that layer's raw height-map sample in [0,1], then the four are renormalised to preserve their sum so the meadow/Grass REMAINDER (1 - sum(stored)) is unchanged. Where two stored layers overlap, the higher-elevation surface wins; a zero-height texel keeps a floor weight (eps) instead of vanishing. k=0 disables the reweighting (absent block behaves identically).
height_blend._height_source: The RAW height sample (0..1), NOT the displacement-centred value. An even power (k=4) applied to a re-centred height (which straddles 0) would fold a texel far BELOW its own mean onto one far above, which is not a height blend. The desk lever wrote 'centred height'; centring is a displacement-only transform and cannot feed (h+eps)**k -- recorded as an intentional interpretation, see LESSONS.
height_blend._bake_lookup_divergence_RESOLVED: F2 (audit + cloud review) RULED by Ryan 2026-09-23: MEASURE, then accept (<=2%) or model (>2%). Measured offline on the real weightmap, walkable area only (research/brief7/input/f2_argmax_flip.json): the raw argmax flips on 3.12% of walkable texels (> 2%), margins p50 0.35 -- so MODELLED. bake_surface_lookup.py now applies the same reweight (same _cpu_height_blend, same k/eps, heights sampled at the texel's world position under each layer's tiling) before its argmax, so the footstep/surface answer matches the painted surface by construction. The surface lookup PNG (textures/alpine_8k_surface.png) must be RE-BAKED with --write during Phase 1, in sync with the material rebuild, so the shipped lookup carries the modelled dominant.

card._why: BRIEF 3 TASK 4, 2026-09-13. hue_percent and brightness_amp are the ruled +/-8%, driven by PerInstanceRandom; brightness rides frac(r*7.31) so it does not track hue (one PerInstanceRandom is ONE scalar per instance). ground_tint 1.0 applies the underlying Grass layer albedo at the INSTANCE position (ObjectPositionWS, not per-pixel, so a card takes one colour from the ground it stands on), at the Grass layer's own 5.03 m tile. ground_albedo_mean 0.038457 is the MEASURED linear-luma mean of WildGrass_C (4096 square, sRGB decoded); dividing by it makes the tint RESHADE rather than darken -- the ratio averages 1.0. contact_darkness 0.55 over the lower contact_height 0.333 is the ground-contact gradient so soil reads through between blades. rock_scatter._saturation_note: DERIVED FROM THE FIELD, NOT TYPED (ruled 2026-09-26). With the router on the 16 m landform (rock_scatter.py landform_height; run 1: research/brief7/rocks_dryrun2.log, 1953 steps, p99 2.003) the deposit value that exactly 305.4 ha of cells exceed -- R12 4a's apron reference, resolution-independent as an AREA -- is 0.102951; p > 0.2 <=> deposit > 0.2231 * saturation, so saturation = 0.102951 / 0.2231 = 0.4615. History: 0.03 (tuned at 4 m) -> 0.001875 (a /16 dilution guess that did not restore the raw-surface field: apron 88.0 -> 112.6 ha; the raw 1 m surface funnelled fans into pits, max 17,488.8, p99 0.045) -> the router change, then this derivation. SCOPE: read by exclude_talus_above and the report's apron p; each talus mask reads its own mask.saturation, held at the ratified RATIO to this value (TalusField/B/C 5/3, TalusChannel 4/3) -- two copies of one number, NN19, owed a single source.
rock_scatter._max_steps_note: RESOLUTION-DEPENDENT, and the ONLY member of this block that is not a property of rock. It is a solver ITERATION BUDGET denominated in CELLS. talus_deposit decays carried mass by trans=exp(-spacing_m/L) per step, so at 1 m spacing mass decays 0.83%/step where 4 m spacing decays 3.3%, and the starting supply is 16x larger on 16x the cells. 600 (tuned at 2017) refused to converge at 8129 with 108.2550 units still in transit; ~1450 are needed and 2400 = 600 x (8129/2017) gives margin. SCALE THIS WITH 1/spacing.

The FinalImage card value at this solve is RECORDED BESIDE IT AND NOT TARGETED, because FinalImage is the LOOK instrument: it carries white balance, tint and the grade, which is what makes it the right place to judge those and the wrong place to solve exposure.
exposure._compensation_at_render_warmup_on: RE-SOLVED 2026-09-13 once RENDER warm-up was actually enabled. ⛔ EVERY CAPTURE BEFORE THIS PROJECT DATE RAN WITH ZERO RENDERED WARM-UP FRAMES: `render_warm_up_count` defaulted to 32 but `render_warm_up_frames` -- the BOOL that gates it -- defaulted to FALSE, while the sidecar recorded a warm-up of 300. That 300 is the ENGINE count, which ticks the game thread and renders nothing. Turning render warm-up on moved the card 0.180 (predicted by the warm-up-off slope model) to 0.216851, about +0.27 EV. Re-solve: correction -log2(0.216851/0.18) = -0.2687 EV DELIVERED, which at the measured slope 0.7196 is -0.3734 REQUESTED -> -14.2554. MEASURED after applying: card 0.179812 against a 0.18 target, band [0.171, 0.189] -- PASS, the first time this bench's card has landed in band.
exposure._compensation_resolved_at_manual: R-METER, RULED 2026-09-12b: RE-SOLVED at Manual metering with Apply Physical Camera Exposure OFF. OLD -4.1268, correction -7.1412, NEW -11.2680. MEASURED per R-GREYCARD on the SCENE-LINEAR EXR: card luma 25.408342 against a 0.18 target, so correction = -log2(25.408342/0.18) = -7.1412. Linearity evidenced by the frame itself -- frame_max_linear 74.5625 EXCEEDS display white, which a tonemapped frame cannot, and disable_tone_curve read back true. WHY IT MOVED SO FAR: with the physical-camera term removed, the scene came back 4-5 stops hot and the capture's own content gate REFUSED it (near_ground luma 0.9576, 57.0% featureless against 0.8% predicted sky). benchmark.json records that exact signature historically -- 'the first ever target run came back 4-5 stops over-exposed, near_ground luma 0.95'. So the old -4.1268 was never a clean exposure: it was a manual bias silently multiplied by the camera's aperture, shutter and ISO, and it only looked right because the two errors cancelled.
exposure._apply_physical_camera_exposure: R-METER, RULED 2026-09-12b: Apply Physical Camera Exposure OFF, so Exposure is exactly 1 over 2^compensation and nothing multiplies it. MEASURED before this key existed: the volume read auto_exposure_apply_physical_camera_exposure TRUE with its override_ companion FALSE -- the ENGINE DEFAULT was in force and the volume asserted nothing either way. An unasserted default is not a setting; it is whatever the engine prefers this version, and it silently scales the manual bias by the camera's aperture, shutter and ISO. perception._what: Declared camera and pixel thresholds from which foliage cull distances are DERIVED. Replaces authored cull_distance_m as the source of truth. BRIEF 1 measured that every authored cull deleted an object while it was still 15-63 px tall, and four of them deleted trees inside the DETAIL band.

declared_camera._note: RULED 2026-09-05: derive at 4K, verify at 1440p. 8K is an inspection tool, not a camera.

thresholds_px._note: vanish: below the render's own Nyquist limit. silhouette: ~2-3 cycles across the object at the CSF peak, where a flat blob of the right colour is indistinguishable from the mesh. detail: ~1 arcmin acuity over a ~40 arcmin object, where internal structure is resolvable. BRIEF 1 section 2.

perception._fade_seconds: Any band transition is dithered over >= 0.35 s. At a 1.4 m/s walk that is a 0.5 m fade band in distance -- trivial in space, decisive in time, because it moves the switch's energy out of the 5-10 Hz band the temporal CSF watches.
perception._cull_ceiling: RULED 2026-09-11 (R-RANGE at 512): every DERIVED cull clamps to the streaming block's main range -- the detail band ends where the world streams out, and a larger cull is dead code. A POINTER, not a number: place_foliage._cull_cm_for reads the streaming block, so a future range ruling re-derives the culls by construction. At 512 m this clamps Conifer (1148.6), ConiferPine (875.0) and SpruceSub (743.5). NOTE the ground-cover gap WIDENED with the 256->512 change: Meadow's authored 50 m cull now leaves 50-512 m unrepresented (was 50-256). The 2026-09-09 ruling (ground cover keeps authored culls; needs a REPRESENTATION below, not a different cull) stands; the BACKLOG'd representation work is more pressing, not different.
perception._cull_threshold: Which threshold the CULL sits at. `detail` is ruled for trees because the next band down is now occupied: HLOD MeshApproximate proxies exist for all 1,042 Merged cells as of 2026-09-09, and SpruceSub and ScotsPineTall ship imposters. *** GROUND COVER IS NOT COVERED BY THAT ARGUMENT. *** HLOD proxies only activate BEYOND the World Partition streaming range (256 m, RuntimePartition.cpp:27), so a Meadow culled at its detail boundary of 18.6 m is absent from 18.6 m to 256 m with nothing representing it. The brief's own rule is that a cull may only sit at a band boundary WHERE THE NEXT BAND EXISTS. Derived values are recorded for every species. RULED 2026-09-09 by Ryan: GROUND COVER KEEPS ITS AUTHORED CULLS -- Meadow 50 m, Blueberry 45 m. The `silhouette` alternative is CLOSED, not deferred: Meadow's silhouette boundary is 123.8 m, still inside the 256 m streaming range, so it would narrow the gap without closing it. Ground cover needs a REPRESENTATION in the band below, not a different cull; BACKLOG carries that as separate work. The ground-cover species keep their authored culls and are marked as such in the sidecar.
perception._derived_by: scripts/place_foliage.py, using scripts/angular_budget.py's dist_for_pixels.
